text: Read the case-let and answer the following- Mitigating climate change means reducing the flow of heat-trapping greenhouse gases into the atmosphere. This involves cutting greenhouse gases from main sources such as power plants factories, cars, and farms. Forests, oceans, and soil also absorb and store these gases, and are an important part of the solution. Reducing and avoiding our emissions requires us to reshape everything we do — from how we power our economy and grow our food, to how we travel and live, and the products we consume. It is a problem felt locally and globally. In the past decades, the EU took firm action against climate change, resulting in a more than 37% drop in EU emissions in 2023 compared with 1990 levels. This is mainly a result of a growing use of renewable energy and decreased use of carbon-intensive fossil fuels. Improvements in energy efficiency and structural changes in the economy also contributed to meeting these goals. Now more ambitious goals are set that include a net 55% or greater reduction below 1990 levels by 2030 and a climate-neutrality objective by 2050. Reaching these goals will require even higher emission cuts through transitioning from fossil fuels to clean, renewable energy. It also means halting deforestation, using land sustainably and restoring nature until we reach the point where the release of greenhouse gases into the atmosphere is balanced with the capture and storage of these gases in our forests, oceans and soil. The EU emits 6% of global emissions and cannot act alone. Global cooperation is essential for all climate change mitigation. The United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and the Paris Agreement ensure cooperation across borders to tackle climate change and ensure a sustainable future. The annual EEA check-up on EU progress on its energy and climate targets stresses that EU Member States will need to sustain this rate of progress to achieve Europe’s climate and energy targets. Source-European Environment Agency, 2025,Report

subject: Global Environment Management
text: Read the given case- study and answer the following question. Tata Steel, one of India’s leading steel producers, faced challenges such as high energy consumption, carbon emissions, and waste generation. Due to increasing environmental regulations and investor pressure, the company integrated corporate sustainability into its environmental management strategy. Tata Steel invested in energy-efficient technologies, renewable energy, and waste heat recovery systems to reduce emissions. It adopted water conservation measures such as rainwater harvesting, zero-liquid-discharge systems, and water recycling. The company also followed a circular economy approach by converting industrial waste like slag into construction materials, minimizing landfill use. Transparent reporting and environmental audits improved accountability. Although these measures required significant initial investment, the company achieved long- term benefits including lower operational costs, regulatory compliance, improved brand image, stronger investor confidence, and better community relations. Source-Corporate Sustainability Practices at Tata Steel, Compiled from Tata Steel Sustainability and Integrated Reports,2025 A) Evaluate the effectiveness of corporate sustainability practices adopted by Tata Steel in managing environmental challenges. B ) Design an additional corporate sustainability strategy that Tata Steel could implement to further strengthen environmental management and long-term profitability.
